speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Government will roll out schemes to incentivise SMEs to pivot to renting electric vehicles for commercial use, in view of Singapore’s Green Plan and climate ambitions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is whether there are any specific sectors he is targeting for the electric vehicle (EV) transition for both motor vehicles as well as motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second is with regard to EV motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just yesterday, I had a resident who is an SME owner and trying to sell electric motorcycles in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: He has concerns about the ability to rent out his motorcycles for commercial use or even private use going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question is whether the Minister can shed some light on which agencies would be appropriate to help such approaches in terms of renting electric motorcycles in Singapore going forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The answer is no, but with an important qualifier.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Basically, because when you make a transition from Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) to electric, there is a general benefit to the overall ecosystem in terms of emissions reduction.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In addition, I would say it is also a function of technology because, for example, in the realm of very heavy vehicles, adoption and usage have been varied when it comes to electrification.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, other solutions, like hydrogen, appear to be gathering momentum.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the second point on EV motorcycles, I must first point out that, today, plug-in solutions already exist.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There are motorcycles that can use plug-in recharging and so on, and that already is there.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But this, generally, tends to be in the higher power output type of motorbikes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For the broad mass, at the moment, there are different models.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because we want to ensure that if batteries can, in fact, be removed from the vehicle and taken to whichever premises, including residential premises, then the attendant risks, including fire hazards, increase as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And so, we want to be very careful about this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What we have done is to commence some trials with partners.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, it brings together the supplier of the motorcycle, the supplier of the charging solution, the user of such motorcycles, like a delivery company and so on, and we have two such trials taking place.
